title: Pro-etale evaluation over an algebraically closed field
statement: Use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Z=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-scheme]. The functor $S\mapsto Z[S]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor] identifies sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with sheaves on profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings. Under this identification, the inverse image $p_Z^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] is the identity on sheaves on profinite sets, and evaluation at $Z$ is evaluation at the one-point profinite set. Every pro-etale covering of $Z$ admits a section through one member. Evaluation at $Z$ is exact on abelian sheaves, and on sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over any ring sheaf $R$ it preserves finite free modules and cokernels, with values in modules over $R(Z)$. For every extension $K\subseteq K'$ of algebraically closed fields, scheme inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] corresponds to the identity under these profinite-site identifications, and therefore canonically preserves evaluation at the final object. These identifications are compatible with composition and with ring and module structures.

source.place: Example 4.2.11 and Example 4.1.10 (profinite-site equivalence); evaluation/exactness and algebraically closed extension compatibility are consequences of this site identification, not assertions of conservativity of geometric points.

proof.text: Apply geometricFieldProfiniteDenseSubsite to the specified test functor. Mathlib Functor.IsDenseSubsite supplies its restriction equivalences for Type (u+1), Ab and RingCat. The prescribed point and abelian point adjunctions have these right adjoints, so their units and counits are isomorphisms. No alternative inverse image is chosen.

The singleton profinite object is terminal. The specified functor preserves finite limits, so its singleton image is terminal. The structural morphism geometricFieldTestFinalMap is consequently an isomorphism to the terminal pro-etale object. For every ring sheaf, apply isEquivalence_pushforward_of_dense to the set and abelian restriction equivalences and the cover-density part of the dense-subsite theorem. Its identity scalar map is exactly geometricFieldModuleRestriction.

For the split-cover assertion, bypass the profinite classification. A pro-etale covering of Spec K has a member containing a point above its unique point. The already proved source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.exists_comp_eq_id_of_weaklyEtale gives a section of that member. Downward closure then puts the identity in every covering sieve. Applied to a generated presieve, its witness is precisely a split generator. This is the private lemma geometricField_cover_id and the first conjunct of geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_exact.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, coverings of the singleton and their sections

proof.text: For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_exact, local injectivity and local surjectivity of the sheafification unit yield covering equalizer and image sieves. By the split-cover assertion these contain the identity, so the unit is bijective on final-object sections. Its evaluation is consequently an isomorphism. Presheaf evaluation preserves colimits, and the reflective sheafification adjunction cancels its left adjoint to show that sheaf evaluation preserves colimits. Finite limits follow from sheafToPresheaf and pointwise evaluation. For arbitrary ring-sheaf modules, use the proved source instance SheafOfModules.preservesColimitsOfShape_toSheaf; the forgetful functor from modules over R(Spec K) to abelian groups reflects colimits. This proves cokernels and the finite free coproduct assertions, with no hypothesis on R and including rank zero. No separate epimorphism/local-surjectivity theorem is used.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, exact evaluation on the singleton; Stacks sites-modules.tex Tag 03CN (lemma-abelian-abelian), part (5), and sites.tex Tag 00WM (definition-sheaves-injective-surjective)

proof.text: For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_extension, use the already specified geometricFieldTestBaseChange, a pullback-composition isomorphism for relative test objects, rather than reconstructing scalar extension on locally constant functions. It identifies restriction after scheme direct image with the restriction on the source. The sets, abelian and ring restriction equivalences from geometric_field_proetale_evaluation therefore imply that scheme direct image is an equivalence, by cancellation of an equivalence on the right. The prescribed adjunction unit is an isomorphism. Whiskering it and composing with the specified test-object and final-object isomorphisms proves both comparisons are isomorphisms. This is proved generically in geometricField_comparisons_isIso and applied to the three coefficient categories. It needs no algebraicity or finiteness of the extension.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, scalar-extension compatibility of the explicit profinite basis

proof.text: For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_coherence, apply the unit equation for conjugate adjunction morphisms to the canonical inverse-image composition comparison, componentwise. Naturality of the two units and of that comparison gives geometricField_comparison_comp for arbitrary schemes, coefficient categories and chosen site maps. At the final object, uniqueness of maps into the pulled-back final object identifies the composite site map. On profinite test objects, prove the same identity by the two pullback projections, using the definitions of geometricFieldTestBaseChange and Over.pullbackComp. Naturality of the unit also gives singleton normalization. For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_identity, apply the same conjugate-unit equation to the identity comparison; naturality and the inverse identities of Over.pullbackId give the evaluated identity. Over.pullbackComp_id_left identifies its site map with geometricFieldTestBaseChange of the identity. For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_operations, base change preserves finite limits and is representably flat, so left Kan extension followed by sheafification preserves finite limits of set-valued sheaves. Naturality of geometricFieldEvaluationComparison at the operation and each product projection is exactly the two required equations. Empty finite families and arbitrary module actions require no separate assumptions. These three theorems are independent of the site-equivalence theorem.
